Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City
Clerk's Office. For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public
comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City Clerk
at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmembers wished the public a Happy New Year.

  Councilmember Brotman asked staff to provide a brief update on how Glendale’s homeless
  population has fared during the storm and what the City is doing to help. Community Services
  and Parks Director Onnig Bulanikian indicated that the Ascencia and Glendale Police
  outreach teams have been offering services such as temporary shelters through the City’s
  hotel voucher program and the Ascencia shelter to the city’s unhoused homeless population.
  Currently the 45-bed Ascencia hotel is at a full capacity so the city has been referring
  individuals to the winter shelter program in Pacoima where they have 65 beds. The City
  currently has a number of individuals who are service resistant, and they are approached by
  City staff once or twice a week who would attempt to convince them to receive services.

  Brotman shared a story of a group of parents from Franklin Elementary, led by Monica
  Campagna and Karen Neilsen, who were concerned that lunch foodware was being used
  once and thrown away. They worked with Glendale Unified school District and the Hobart
  company to pilot a dishwashing program at the school so students can use regular plates,
  utensils, and cups. The success of the pilot program led the parents to approach Senator
  Portantino and ask him to carry a bill that would fund a statewide program to replicate this
  across the state. Although the bill did not pass, CA Governor Newsom took notice and set
  aside $15M to fund this program that will help approximately 375 schools shift to reusable
  foodware, serving up to 225,000 students. Brotman expressed that it was great that so many
  students will now learn about reusable foodware and take this knowledge home to their
  parents. He also noted how a few concerned and committed community members can make
  a difference. He commended the efforts of the Franklin Elementary parents and committed
  citizens who worked to make this possible. He thanked GUSD for being willing to make some
  changes, Sen. Portantino for bringing the idea to Sacramento and Governor Newsom for
  carving out the money to take this program statewide.

  Councilmember Asatryan asked staff to provide a report about formalizing a program and
  partnership with GUSD where Glendale Water and Power and Sustainability Office will work
  with GUSD students to institute an educational program regarding waste management and
  proper recycling. City Manager Roubik Golanian informed council that there was a program in
  place but it was put on hold because of the pandemic. Since the students are now back in
  school, this program could be brought back to the schools and a report of this program will be
  presented to council soon. Asatryan travelled to Armenia during the holidays to visit Glendale
  sister cities, Gyumri and Ghapan, but she was not able to visit Martuni in the Republic of
  Artsakh, due to the Azerbaijani blockade. She was happy to report that both Gyumri and
  Ghapan want to re-establish strong ties with the City of Glendale, as there are a lot of
  opportunities for the cities to work together and collaborate. She stated that the City of Gyumri

  3
   is leading the way in clean energy projects, and they have reached a point where all their
  government and school facilities are now utilizing 100% clean energy and are looking for ways
  to do better waste management. Asatryan stated that the City of Ghapan is in an area where
  there are Azerbaijani military posts, and some parts of the region, which were in Armenia
  proper, are now occupied by Azerbaijan. Asatryan visited the Ghapan Museum where she
  viewed a section that was dedicated to the Glendale and Ghapan Sister City Association. The
  City of Gyumri is also looking into opening a museum that would highlight their sister cities
  and they were hoping that the City of Glendale could provide some items that they can include
  in their museum. Asatryan stated that the Mayor of Ghapan would like to formally invite the
  City of Glendale for a delegation visit. She also extended a similar invitation to the City of
  Ghapan. Asatryan visited the Yerevan City Council Meeting as an honorary guest. One of the
  items discussed at the meeting was their Al Fresco program. The City of Yerevan currently
  has 26,000 permits for renovations and build-out and their process requires a 15-day
  turnaround. If a permit has not been issued within this timeframe, the applicant has the right to
  build whatever they want. One of the things that the City of Yerevan has asked for was
  collaboration and assistance on Emergency Preparedness since it is an issue all across
  Armenia and Artsakh.

  Mayor Kassakhian stated it was great to be back after a peaceful and uneventful holiday and
  hoped that everyone was able to observe and celebrate the season. He stated that he
  attended several events last week in observance of the Armenian Orthodox Christmas
  including the blessings of the water ceremonies at Glendale Memorial Hospital and Glendale
  Adventist Hospital. Due to the rainy season, Kassakhian informed the residents that staff was
  asked to keep an eye and address issues that may arise at the Rockhaven building. He
  announced that the city will be closed on Monday in observance of Martin Luther King, Jr.
  Day. He spoke about the importance of the holiday for Americans as it is a reminder of the
  struggles that so many have had to fight and the challenges of discrimination that people in
  our country had to endure until those rights were outlined in the constitution and were
  accessible to all. He also read an excerpt from the speech Dr. King gave in Oslo, in 1964,
  during his acceptance of the Nobel Peace Prize.
